author: manunlp
content:
[validator.md](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/pq/specs/_features/pq/validator.md#vrf-tree) only says the VRF leaves are "secret random values, one for each slot". It gives no derivation.
A validator registers its VRF root once and it can't change it afterwards. Each block it proposes must reveal a leaf of the tree behind that root.
If the validator moves to a client that derives the tree differently, that client builds another tree with another root. Its RANDAO reveals then fail verification and its blocks are invalid.

LH and Prysm already disagree on that:

- [Lighthouse](https://github.com/ethDreamer/lighthouse/blob/pq/beacon_node/genesis/src/pq.rs):
  - `seed = sha256("vrf-seed" ‖ bls_sk), leaf[i] = sha256(seed ‖ uint64_le(i))`
  - only the first 2^20 leaves are filled.
- [Prysm](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/lean-xmss-vrf-tree/validator/vrftree/tree.go):
  - `vrf_seed = sha256(xmss_seed ‖ "VRF_SEED"), leaf[i] = sha256(vrf_seed ‖ uint_to_bytes32(i))`
  - all 2^31 leaves are filled.

The same validator gets a different VRF root in each client.

Should I open a PR on the spec repo to specify that?
(cc <@592004585506340885>)

author: barnabasbusa
content:
Quick question for client teams: for devnets, do you want to LOAD precomputed XMSS/VRF material, or COMPUTE it in your client at startup?

Why it matters: every validator needs an expanded XMSS key and a VRF tree before it can sign. Here is what that costs for one kurtosis run on an 18-core laptop:

```
                               64 validators    1000 validators
Genesis (pubkeys + VRF roots)
  compute                      ~35 s            ~9 min   (measured)
  load from file               instant          instant  (measured)

Validator clients (secret side)
  compute XMSS keys            ~20 s            ~5 min
  compute VRF tree, 2^20       ~8 s             ~2 min
  compute VRF tree, 2^31       ~16 min          ~4 hours
  load precomputed             a download       a download
                               (~200 MB?)       (~3 GB?)
```

author: barnabasbusa
content:
Ask for LH and Prysm so pq devnets start fast from ethereum-package:

**Problem:** since spec commit 2f43bc0 the VRF tree is Keccak over all 2^31 leaves. One root is ~4.3 billion hashes, minutes of a whole machine per validator, so nobody can build it at startup.

**What we have:** all 10,000 keys of the default kurtosis mnemonic precomputed on a 5090 (~0.75 s/key) and shipped in ethereum-package. consensoor loads them at startup and finalizes on full 2^31 trees.

**What we need:** one flag per client, e.g. `--vrf-state-url <file url>`. The package will pass it to every client that supports it.
- File: 1028 bytes per key index = VRF root (32) | slot u32 LE, always 0 (4) | 31 siblings of leaf 0, bottom-up (992)
- Supports HTTP Range: fetch `index * 1028` for your validators, check the root against `state.validators[i].vrf_root`
- Keep the top 11 siblings (heights 20..30), build the bottom 2^20 leaves from the seed locally, serve proofs from that. Covers 2^20 slots.

**Next:** same idea for XMSS signing keys, a 1,476-byte compact state instead of rebuilding trees.

**PRs (same encoding in Go and Rust):**
VRF: <https://github.com/nalepae/go-leanxmss/pull/2> <https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/795>
XMSS: <https://github.com/nalepae/go-leanxmss/pull/1> <https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/794>

**Conventions:** vrf_seed = sha256("vrf-seed" || BLS sk), leaf i = keccak256(vrf_seed || uint64_le(i)), node = keccak256(left || right)

Reference: consensoor `pq` (`--vrf-state-url`), ethereum-package `pq` (`vrf_state_url`). File link to follow.

author: barnabasbusa
content:
Fair, there shouldn't be any BLS in a pq test. Right now it's only there as a container: devnet tooling still hands clients the usual BLS keystores, and we hash that 32-byte secret into the XMSS seed and the VRF seed. Nothing is signed or verified with BLS.
We should drop it and derive straight from the mnemonic, all Keccak:
seed_i = keccak256("pq-validator" || bip39_seed || uint64_le(i))
xmss_seed = keccak256("leanxmss-seed" || seed_i)
vrf_seed = keccak256("vrf-seed" || seed_i)
Clients would then load a plain per-validator seed file instead of a BLS keystore. That removes sha256 from the seed too.
